extracted.intended_audience: authors, peer reviewers, journal editors, statisticians, epidemiologists and clinical researchers working on multivariable prediction model studies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reporting studies that develop, validate, or update multivariable clinical prediction (prognostic or diagnostic) models so that reports are transparent, complete, and usable by other researchers and clinicians.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPOD checklist (22 essential items)
rubrics_metrics.description: The TRIPOD Statement is an annotated checklist ... The resulting checklist comprises 22 items that were regarded essential for good reporting of studies developing or validating multivariable prediction models. Authors of published reports of studies describing the development, validation or updating of a prediction model should ensure that all items in the checklist are mentioned somewhere in the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checklist is available as a PDF/Word; authors should mention all items somewhere in the article. The checklist arose from systematic review and a 3-day consensus meeting with international experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide full information on the actual model
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must provide information on the actual model so that other researchers are able to use the model to test the model or use on their patients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The blog emphasises that many articles failed to provide model details and that published articles with incomplete reporting are unusable. Report model equation/parameters and enough detail for external use and testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent and complete reporting to enable evaluation, implementation, and synthesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Without full and transparent reporting, evaluating, even implementing and synthesizing the results from such studies is problematic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparent reporting should provide the 'crucial information' needed for readers to critique, judge, implement, and include studies in evidence syntheses (see CHARMS checklist reference).

rubrics_metrics.name: State study type clearly: development, validation, or updating
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports should clearly describe whether the study is developing, validating or updating a prediction model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TRIPOD is intended for reporting studies describing development, validation or updating of prediction models; corresponding checklist items should be addressed for the relevant study type.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPOD is guidance for reporting, not prescriptive methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: The recommendations within TRIPOD are guidelines only for reporting research and do not prescribe how to develop or validate a prediction model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TRIPOD should not be used to dictate methodological choices; it focuses on what to report rather than how investigators must conduct their modelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use TRIPOD as a quality assessment tool — use PROBAST for risk of bias
rubrics_metrics.description: The checklist is not a quality assessment tool to gauge the quality of a multivariable prediction model, for which the upcoming PROBAST risk of bias tool will be available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate tools exist for assessing methodological quality/risk of bias; TRIPOD's purpose is reporting completeness and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and brevity appropriate to varied technical audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide guidance that can be readily understood by study investigators of varying levels of technical (e.g. methodological) experience; keep the checklist as brief as possible while ensuring key details are reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To encourage uptake by authors, peer reviewers and editors, the checklist was kept concise and worded to be accessible across differing levels of methodological expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide an Explanation & Elaboration companion with rationale and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: An accompanying and extensive Explanation & Elaboration article discusses rationale and examples of good reporting and methodological aspects for investigators to consider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The E&E article (~22,000 words) gives examples, discusses competing methodological approaches with advantages/disadvantages, and cautions against methodologically weak approaches, aiming to be neutral rather than prescriptive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage journal endorsement and requirement of checklist submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals should endorse TRIPOD by including prediction model studies as a distinct study type, include TRIPOD in their instructions for authors and require authors to complete and submit a TRIPOD Checklist in their submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co-publication in leading journals and listing endorsing journals on the TRIPOD website are recommended strategies to increase uptake and visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make checklist and resources openly available and visible
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the checklist and supporting material (PDF/Word) on a dedicated website and publicise via networks and social media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TRIPOD resources are hosted at www.tripod-statement.org; endorsing journals and additional information should be listed to facilitate access and adoption.
